title: Coefficient order locus and regular coefficient-transform data
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $X,M$ schemes, $p:M\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $i:X\to M$, $a\in X$, $m,n,s,Q\in\mathbf N$, $\alpha:\{0,\ldots,s-1\}\to\mathbf N^n$, and $D$ a specified regular Hilbert coefficient datum for these parameters [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum], with chart $e:U\to M$, coefficient scheme $j:N\hookrightarrow U$ and coefficients $c_{l\gamma}$. Put $d_l=|\alpha_l|$. Its coefficient order locus is the subset $S_D=\{z\in N:\operatorname{germ}_z(c_{l\gamma})\in\mathfrak m_z^{d_l-|\gamma|}\text{ for every }l,\gamma\text{ with }|\gamma|<d_l\}$, where $\mathfrak m_z$ is the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{N,z}$. For an empty vertex list this is all of $N$.
Let $J\subset\mathcal O_N$ be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf defining a closed subscheme of $N$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $C\subset U$ be its image under $j$. Write $\pi:U'\to U$ for the blowup of $C$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], $X'\to U'$ for the scheme-theoretic strict transform of $X\times_M U\to U$, and $j':N'\to U'$ for the scheme-theoretic strict transform of $j$ [def-nagata-strict-transform]. Write $\rho:N'\to N$ for its canonical map. For any $x'\in X'$, a regular coefficient transform of $D,J$ at $x'$ consists of a regular Hilbert coefficient datum $D'$ for $X'\to U'$ at $x'$ over $k$, with the same $m,n,s,\alpha,Q$, together with a map $q:N_{D'}\to N'$ whose square with $N_{D'}\hookrightarrow U_{D'}$, $j':N'\to U'$ and $e_{D'}:U_{D'}\to U'$ is cartesian, and a regular function $h\in\Gamma(N_{D'},\mathcal O_{N_{D'}})$. The pullback of the ideal of $C$ along $N_{D'}\to U_{D'}\to U'\to U$ is required to be the principal ideal $(h)$. For every $l,\gamma$, its coefficients satisfy $h^{d_l-|\gamma|}c'_{l\gamma}=(\rho\circ q)^*c_{l\gamma}$ when $|\gamma|<d_l$, and $c'_{l\gamma}=h^{|\gamma|-d_l}(\rho\circ q)^*c_{l\gamma}$ otherwise. These are specifications of data and properties; neither existence of such a transform nor a Hilbert-function equality criterion is asserted.
